messages:
Alex: FYI - noticed a ~20% p99 latency regression on canary after merge of #5123. Canary autoslo flagged and rollout stopped automatically.
DeployBot: Canary rollout paused for release/2026-03-18-5123 due to latency SLO violation (p99 > 250ms) :rotating_light:
Alex: Repro in perf-ci as well — CI perf job shows tail latency jump on 5123 build.
Mira: what's in that PR again? I remember it touched kernel selection heuristics.
Sam: It changed kernel priority to prefer the fused attention kernel for short seqs and bumped continuous batching window from 10ms -> 25ms. Also a small KV cache eviction tweak (ttl trim on shard recycle).
Jamie: can we get a quick flamegraph/prof on canary traces? I ran a few traces and saw more time in memory copy + kernel dispatch.
Alex: attaching short trace from perf-ci run:
```
# perf snapshot p99
seq=16: kernel=fused_attn  -> avg 4.8ms -> 6.2ms
seq=256: kernel=blocked_attn -> avg 12ms -> 11.8ms
kv_hit_ratio dropped 92% -> 74%
batch_wait increased median 8ms -> 18ms
```
Mira: kv_hit_ratio drop is huge. Did the ttl trim cause aggressive evictions? That would hurt cache hits and increase expensive recompute.
Sam: correct — the shard recycle path had an off-by-one where we started clearing buckets earlier than intended. On heavy tail workloads that increases kv churn.
DeployBot: CI-Robot reported perf test 2026-03-18T09:12:03: build 5123 failed perf gate: p99 latency +21% vs baseline.
Priya: can we isolate whether fused_attn kernel itself regressed or whether it's just more misses + bigger batches causing scheduling overhead?
Jamie: I ran a microbenchmark of fused_attn kernel in isolation — latency is fine. The extra memcpy was from larger KV payloads per request (more sequence prefixes uncached).
Sam: root cause looks like a combination: KV eviction bug + increased batching window. The batching change increases in-flight token batches and stresses the cache eviction path.
Alex: propose revert of kernel heuristic + revert the batching window increase as a quick mitigation. Then follow up with a fix for kv eviction bug and consider an autoslo guard for KV hit ratio.
Mira: can we instead gate the heuristic behind rollout config param so we don't need a full revert? I want minimal churn in the binary.
Alex: yeah we can toggle via runtime flag in rollout. But rollout config currently uses two variants (A old-heuristic, B new). Canary was trying B and then rolled A->B. The autoslo paused when B surpassed threshold.
Sam: the quick patch I can push: set rollout default to A (safe) and keep B in canary only after fix. Will open PR in ~15m.
Priya: for future: add a perf-ci test that exercises KV hit ratio across seq distribution and fails if hit_ratio drops >5%.
Jamie: agree. Also add a canary check that monitors kv_hit_ratio and treats it as a hard gate. Right now only token latency is gated.
Alex: +1. New guard proposal: require both p99 latency and kv_hit_ratio >= baseline-5% for promotion. Also add a dynamic rollback: if kv_hit_ratio drops >8% for 5m straight, rollback automatically.
Mira: sounds good. Does the rollout system support composite gates today?
Sam: not fully; we have hooks for custom metrics but no short declarative policy. We can implement a small plugin that queries telemetry and returns pass/fail.
Alex: action items:
- Sam: open quick rollback PR to pin rollout to A (safe) -> ready in 15m. (assignee Sam)
- Sam: fix kv eviction off-by-one in separate PR, add unit test (KV test). (assignee Sam)
- Jamie: add perf-ci regression test for kv_hit_ratio distribution. (assignee Jamie)
- Priya: spec composite canary gate (latency + kv_hit_ratio) and implement plugin. (assignee Priya)
- Mira: monitor canary traces and re-run perf-ci once quick revert lands.
Sam: PR 5127 opened to set rollout default back to A and add flag. Will tag @alex and request fast review.
Alex: thx. once PR merges, we'll let the canary resume and watch telemetry for 30m before re-promoting.
Jamie: also adding a short doc blurb to eng-runtime runbook about KV eviction metrics to watch.
Priya: question — do we want automatic revert to happen at the control-plane level or let deploy pipeline perform the revert? Automatic rollback in control plane seems safer for fast failures.
Mira: I prefer control-plane auto-rollback for SLOs, but require a manual confirmation for infra-impacting reverts. We should also email on rollback.
Alex: agreed. For now, control-plane auto-pause + ops notification. We'll iterate to full auto-rollback once plugin matures.
DeployBot: Rollout resume is blocked until PR 5127 merges and passes CI. Canary remains paused.
Sam: pushed fix branch for KV off-by-one: will add tests and request review by EOD.
Alex: thanks everyone. If canary stays paused beyond 60m without PR, we'll trigger an incident slack thread.
Mira: noted. I'll stand by for traces and will help validate once revert is live. :thumbsup:
CI-Robot: perf-ci run queued for build 5127. Slack notification will follow on completion.
Alex: closing thread — will post final status once canary resumes or we elect to revert fully.
